description: Bundled detection rules for Minecraft Cleaner Pro Ultimate. Every non-heuristic rule cites the public source its indicators were verified against on the date shown. No hashes or indicators were invented. Generated by rules/build_rules.py.

indicators.description: Declares a 'meteor' entrypoint, which only Meteor Client loads

rules.confidenceRationale: Meteor Client add-ons register themselves through a 'meteor' entrypoint in fabric.mod.json, as shown in Meteor's official add-on template. Such a jar only works together with Meteor Client and extends it with more modules. The specific add-on rules (CP-ADDON-0002 and later) name well-known add-ons.
rules.falsePositiveNotes: A few add-ons only add cosmetic or utility features, but all of them require Meteor Client.
rules.limitations: Add-ons for other clients (for example RusherHack plugins) are covered by their own rules.

indicators.description: Mod metadata uses the Meteor Rejects mod id
Classes in the Meteor Rejects package
Meteor Rejects mixin configuration
Meteor add-on entrypoint

rules.confidenceRationale: The identifiers were taken from the official Meteor Rejects source repository (see sources). Two independent indicators are required for a known match; a single indicator is reported as a suspicion or for review. It is a Meteor Client add-on, so Meteor Client itself is usually installed as well.
rules.falsePositiveNotes: Third-party addons for this client reuse its package names. Renamed or repackaged builds may not match. A matching file proves the client is installed, not that it was used on a server.
rules.limitations: Only installed files are detected. Builds that were obfuscated or relocated to other packages are not covered by this rule.

indicators.description: RusherHack plugin manifest

rules.confidenceRationale: RusherHack plugins carry a rusherhack-plugin.json manifest (with Plugin-Class, Name and Minecraft-Versions), as in the official example plugin. A plugin only runs inside the RusherHack hacked client, so finding one strongly suggests RusherHack is used. RusherHack itself is closed source and is matched by name only (CP-HEUR-0005).
rules.falsePositiveNotes: None known: the manifest name is specific to RusherHack.
rules.limitations: The closed-source RusherHack client itself has no published indicators.

indicators.description: Mod metadata uses the Baritone mod id
Baritone mixin configuration

rules.confidenceRationale: Baritone is open-source automation software (LGPL). It is not malware and is allowed on some servers but forbidden on many, so it is only ever reported for review.
rules.falsePositiveNotes: Some legitimate clients bundle Baritone for single-player use.
rules.limitations: Whether Baritone is allowed depends on the server's rules.

indicators.description: Wurst list of enabled hacks
Wurst keybind configuration
Wurst configuration folder

rules.confidenceRationale: WurstClient.java creates a 'wurst' folder in the game directory containing enabled-hacks.json, keybinds.json and other settings. These files show Wurst was installed at some point.
rules.falsePositiveNotes: A folder named 'wurst' could be created by something else; only enabled-hacks.json is treated as a known match.
rules.limitations: Configuration leftovers do not show when, or whether, the client was used.

indicators.description: Meteor Client data folder

rules.confidenceRationale: MeteorClient.java stores its data in a folder named after its mod id ('meteor-client') in the game directory.
rules.falsePositiveNotes: Any program could create a folder with this name.
rules.limitations: Leftover folders do not show when, or whether, the client was used.

indicators.description: Class named like a 'killaura' cheat module inside a module/hack package
Class named like a 'aim' cheat module inside a module/hack package
Class named like a 'triggerbot' cheat module inside a module/hack package
Class named like a 'autoclicker' cheat module inside a module/hack package
Class named like a 'reach' cheat module inside a module/hack package
Class named like a 'velocity' cheat module inside a module/hack package
Class named like a 'criticals' cheat module inside a module/hack package
Class named like a 'crystalaura' cheat module inside a module/hack package
Class named like a 'hitbox' cheat module inside a module/hack package

rules.confidenceRationale: Generic heuristic: hacked clients organise cheats as one class per module inside 'module(s)'/'hack(s)' packages. The verified examples are Meteor Client (systems/modules/combat/KillAura), Wurst (hacks/KillauraHack), BleachHack (module/mods/Killaura), ThunderHack (features/modules/combat/Aura) and LiquidBounce (features/module/modules/combat/killaura/ModuleKillAura). Class names alone are weak evidence. Two distinct combat-module names are needed for review and four for a high-confidence suspicion (KillAura, aim assistance, trigger bots, auto-clickers, reach, velocity/anti-knockback, criticals, crystal aura, hitboxes).
rules.falsePositiveNotes: Legitimate mods occasionally use these words for class names inside 'features' or 'modules' packages. Several distinct module names must appear together before anything is reported, and legitimacy evidence overrides this heuristic.
rules.limitations: Obfuscated clients rename classes and are not found by this heuristic.

rules.family: Known hacked-client name in file name

rules.confidenceRationale: A file name is weak evidence: anyone can name a file anything, so this alone only ever leads to 'Needs review' with a low severity. rules.family: Code loaded through JVM options (Java agent)

indicators.description: JVM option that loads an agent into the game
JVM option that adds classes to the boot class path

rules.confidenceRationale: A Java agent (-javaagent, -agentpath, -agentlib) or a boot class path addition runs extra code inside Minecraft without being in the mods folder. Injected cheats use this, so every such option in launcher settings or in JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS, _JAVA_OPTIONS or JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS (which every Java program reads) is shown for review, and the file it loads is scanned separately.
rules.falsePositiveNotes: Some legitimate tools use agents too, for example authentication helpers for alternative account systems (authlib-injector), profilers and debuggers.
rules.limitations: Agents attached to an already running game, and DLLs injected by other programs, leave no launch option to find.

indicators.description: Stage 0 loader: reflective URLClassLoader download-and-run sequence
Stage 0 variant: Runtime.exec of a Base64-decoded command
Byte array spelling the original stage 0 command-and-control address

rules.confidenceRationale: Instruction sequences published by the fractureiser investigators in nekodetector. Its author describes the first signature as a definite detection and the other two as near-certain and likely detections; they are matched statically without running any code.
rules.falsePositiveNotes: The investigation notes that some early stage 0 scanners produced false positives on popular mods; these signatures are the later, specific ones. The third signature uses strict contiguous matching, which is at least as specific as nekodetector's.
rules.limitations: Only the documented stage 0 variants are recognised. If stage 0 was found, later stages may have run: check the system-artifact findings and run a full antivirus scan.
